title: Pullback of the multiplicative sheaf to a strict henselization
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], put $S_{(\bar x)}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and let $p:X\times_S S_{(\bar x)}\to X$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. The canonical map of etale sheaves $p^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X}\to\mathbf G_{m,X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}}$, adjoint to the pullback-of-units map $\mathbf G_{m,X}\to p_*\mathbf G_{m,X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}}$, is an isomorphism [def-sc-gm-torsor, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

source.place: Theorem Tag 03Q9 proof, identification of units on the qcqs inverse limit (using Tag 09YQ)

proof.text: By the strict-henselization limit definition, the affine pointed etale-neighbourhood index is small and cofiltered. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex], whose statement supplies a nonempty directed set and the same limit cone, and then base change the resulting inverse system along $f$. Thus $X_V=X\times_SV$ has affine transition maps (base changes of the affine transition maps $V'\to V$) and limit $X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]; the assertion that these fibre products commute with the limit is the universal property of fibre products (elementary). The base change $X_V\to V$ of $f$ remains quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3), so each $X_V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by (2) of the same statement, $V$ being affine; likewise $X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}$ is quasi-separated. Finally $p$ is the resulting limit projection by the fibre-product construction [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Theorem Tag 03Q9 proof, passage from affine etale neighbourhoods to the strict henselization limit; Stacks Tag 01YW

proof.text: Let $U\to X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}$ be an affine etale test object; it is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1) ($U$ affine, $X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}$ quasi-separated). Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-data-descent], applied to this particular $U$, gives a stage $V_0$ and an etale morphism of finite presentation $U_0\to X_{V_0}$ with $U\cong U_0\times_{X_{V_0}}(X\times_SS_{(\bar x)})$; put $U_V=U_0\times_{X_{V_0}}X_V$ for $V\ge V_0$, so $U=\varprojlim_VU_V$ (fibre products commute with the limit, elementary as in Step 1) and $U_0$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2). Sections of $p^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X}$: write $q_V:X_V\to X$ for the etale stage maps and $f_V:X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}\to X_V$, $f_{VV_0}:X_V\to X_{V_0}$ for the projections. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (1), $q_V^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X}\cong\mathbf G_{m,X}|_{X_V}=\mathbf G_{m,X_V}$, the last equality because both have sections $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)^\times$ on $W$ etale over $X_V$ [def-sc-gm-torsor]. With $p=q_{V_0}\circ f_{V_0}$ and $q_V=q_{V_0}\circ f_{VV_0}$, [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] (2) gives $p^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X}\cong f_{V_0}^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X_{V_0}}$ and $f_{VV_0}^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X_{V_0}}\cong\mathbf G_{m,X_V}$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-continuity], with $i=j_0=V_0$, $F_{V_0}=\mathbf G_{m,X_{V_0}}$ and $W_{V_0}=U_0$, gives $(p^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X})(U)\cong\varinjlim_V\mathcal O(U_V)^\times$. Units: $U\to S_{(\bar x)}$ is a morphism of affine schemes, hence affine, and it is the base change to the limit of $U_0\to V_0$ (over the affine stage $V_0$; $U_0$, $V_0$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated); so by [lem-weil-pbc-descend-affine] $U_{V_1}\to V_1$ is affine for some $V_1\ge V_0$, hence $U_V$ is affine for all $V\ge V_1$ (affine transition maps). By the affine clause of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], $U=\operatorname{Spec}\varinjlim_{V\ge V_1}\mathcal O(U_V)$, and a unit of a directed colimit of rings together with its inverse comes from a finite stage, so $\varinjlim_V\mathcal O(U_V)^\times\to\mathcal O(U)^\times=\mathbf G_{m,X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}}(U)$ is bijective (elementary). The composite of these bijections is the component on $U$ of the canonical map $p^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,X}\to\mathbf G_{m,X\times_SS_{(\bar x)}}$, since both send the class of $s\in\mathcal O(U_V)^\times$ to its pullback along $U\to U_V$ (the maps $\rho$ of the section-continuity statement are built from the adjunction units, which correspond to pullback of units). A morphism of etale sheaves that is bijective on all affine etale objects is an isomorphism (affine objects cover every object; sheaf axiom, elementary), so the map adjoint to the pullback-of-units map [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] is an isomorphism.
